# Multitenant Isolation & Security Checklist: Pessoa & Beneficiário Multitenant Registry

**Purpose**: Formal pre-implementation gate validating that the spec's requirements around tenant isolation, cross-tenant access denial, and membership enforcement — Constitution Principle I, the NON-NEGOTIABLE guarantee — are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and objectively verifiable before implementation starts.
**Created**: 2026-08-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for every mutation path on a Beneficiário record (create, read, update, delete) with respect to tenant scoping, not just read/delete? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010/FR-011]
- [x] CHK002 Is it specified whether the Beneficiário *listing/search* endpoint carries the same "no cross-tenant data, ever" guarantee that the single-record access requirement (FR-011) states explicitly? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013/FR-014]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for what happens when a user's tenant membership is revoked or changed while they hold an already-issued session/credential? [Gap]
- [x] CHK004 Is there a requirement guaranteeing at least one pre-configured user is restricted to a single tenant, so the "activate a tenant you're not a member of" denial path (FR-021) is actually demonstrable from seed data? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017/FR-021] — Resolved 2026-08-17: FR-017 now also mandates a single-tenant-only seeded user.
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for tenant-enumeration resistance — i.e., does attempting to activate a nonexistent tenant ID behave identically (from the requester's point of view) to attempting to activate a real tenant the user isn't a member of? [Gap, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK006 Are requirements defined for rate-limiting or throttling repeated cross-tenant access attempts (e.g., sequential Beneficiário ID guessing), or is this explicitly declared out of scope? [Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Is "the currently active tenant" precisely defined — i.e., is it unambiguous exactly which piece of request state (vs. a stored server-side session, vs. a client-declared value) determines it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006/FR-015]
- [ ] CHK008 Is "no indication that such a record exists elsewhere" (FR-011) specific enough to rule out subtler leaks, such as timing differences or distinguishable error codes between "record doesn't exist" and "record exists in another tenant"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011]
- [x] CHK009 Is "membership" (as in "the tenants that user is associated with") defined clearly enough to distinguish it from other possible meanings (e.g., ownership, administrative role) elsewhere in the spec? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015/FR-021]
- [x] CHK010 Is the boundary between "denied because the tenant doesn't exist" and "denied because the user isn't a member" clearly and consistently specified across all the places tenant activation is described? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021, Edge Cases]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK011 Is the Pessoa registry's explicit lack of tenant-scoping (User Story 1: global, "independent of any tenant") reconciled with the Beneficiário isolation guarantee — i.e., does the spec make clear that any authorized user, regardless of tenant membership, can view/edit/delete every Pessoa record, including individuals enrolled as Beneficiários in tenants that user has no access to? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities/User Story 1]
- [x] CHK012 Does the Pessoa-deletion-block requirement (FR-005: "explain why the deletion was blocked") risk being inconsistent with the isolation guarantee, by potentially revealing which tenant(s) reference a Pessoa to a user who has no membership in those tenants? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005 vs FR-011] — Resolved via `/speckit-clarify` (2026-08-15): FR-005 now explicitly requires a generic, tenant-agnostic block message; propagated to the Edge Cases bullet, data-model.md, and tasks.md (T028/T032).
- [x] CHK013 Are the isolation guarantees stated consistently between the functional requirements (FR-011, FR-021, FR-024) and the measurable success criteria (SC-003), with no narrower or broader claim in one than the other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011/FR-021/FR-024 vs §SC-003] — Resolved 2026-08-17: added SC-009, giving FR-021 its own dedicated success criterion alongside SC-003.
- [x] CHK014 Is the "tenant is implicit from context, never client-supplied" rule (FR-024) applied uniformly to every Beneficiário write operation described in User Story 2's acceptance scenarios, with no scenario implying a client-supplied tenant value? [Consistency, Spec §FR-024 vs User Story 2]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK015 Is SC-003's "100% of attempts ... are blocked" criterion phrased so it can be objectively tested (i.e., does it enumerate or reference the specific attempt types: view, edit, delete, list, search, direct access)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK016 Is SC-004 ("no leftover data ... remaining on screen") measurable independent of implementation choice — i.e., stated as an observable outcome rather than assuming a particular UI mechanism? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK017 Is there a measurable acceptance criterion specifically for the membership-restriction guarantee (a user cannot even *select* a tenant outside their membership), separate from the record-level isolation criterion (SC-003)? [Gap, Measurability] — Resolved 2026-08-17: SC-009 added.

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for the primary flow (authorized user, valid membership, active tenant matches request) with explicit pass criteria? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 2/3]
- [ ] CHK019 Are requirements defined for the alternate flow of a user with membership in more than two tenants switching between three or more, not just the two-tenant case shown in the acceptance scenarios? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for the exception flow of a request that omits the active-tenant selection entirely (no tenant context at all), as distinct from an invalid/unauthorized tenant selection? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements defined for the recovery flow after a denied cross-tenant attempt — does the user's session/active tenant remain valid and usable, or is any further state defined? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 3 Acceptance Scenario 6]
- [ ] CHK022 Are non-functional (security) requirements for isolation enforcement — e.g., that the check must happen server-side before any data access, never relying on client-side filtering alone — explicitly and separately stated, not just implied by functional requirements? [Coverage, Spec §FR-011/FR-021]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK023 Is the behavior specified for a Beneficiário identifier that is syntactically valid but belongs to no tenant at all (e.g., a deleted or never-existent record) versus one that exists in a foreign tenant — are both required to look identical to the caller? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the behavior specified for a user with zero tenant memberships (e.g., a newly created account not yet assigned to any tenant) attempting any Beneficiário operation? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the behavior specified for concurrent tenant switches by the same user in rapid succession (e.g., two switch requests racing) with respect to which tenant ends up "active"? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [x] CHK026 Is the behavior specified for a matrícula filter or Pessoa-name filter on the Beneficiário listing that could, if mis-scoped, leak the existence of a same-matrícula record in a different tenant (distinct from the direct-ID-access case already covered by FR-011)? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-014 vs FR-011]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK027 Is the assumption that "membership check is the only differentiation within a tenant" (Assumptions: no read-only vs. full-access roles) validated against the isolation requirements — i.e., does the spec confirm this doesn't weaken the cross-tenant guarantee in any way? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK028 Is the dependency on the authentication mechanism correctly identifying the caller (a prerequisite for every tenant-membership check) stated as an explicit assumption, given the spec itself is authentication-mechanism-agnostic? [Dependency, Assumption]
- [x] CHK029 Is the assumption that pre-configured/seed tenants and memberships are sufficient to demonstrate isolation "for review purposes" (Assumptions) cross-checked against CHK004 above (need for a single-tenant-only seeded user)? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions] — Resolved 2026-08-17: self-resolving now that FR-017 (CHK004) mandates the single-tenant seeded user.

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [x] CHK030 Is there any remaining ambiguity about whether "authorized user" (used throughout) always implies "has an active tenant selected," or whether some operations (e.g., Pessoa CRUD) are authorized without any tenant context at all — and is this distinction called out explicitly wherever it matters for isolation? [Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions] — Resolved 2026-08-17: Assumptions now explicitly distinguishes Pessoa operations (sign-in only) from Beneficiário operations (sign-in + active tenant).
- [x] CHK031 Is a requirement & acceptance-criteria ID scheme consistently applied to every isolation-related requirement (FR-011, FR-015, FR-016, FR-017, FR-018, FR-021, FR-024) so each is independently traceable and testable? [Traceability]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- CHK012 and CHK011 surfaced a genuine potential requirements gap (Pessoa-deletion-block message possibly leaking cross-tenant enrollment) — worth resolving via `/speckit-clarify` or a spec amendment before implementation, given Principle I is NON-NEGOTIABLE
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
